description:
We are a team passionate about space, technology, and history. AstroNex is our educational website exploring NASA missions, spacecraft, rovers, satellites, and their discoveries.

Muhammadsaid — Research & documentation.
Sharifkhucha — Coding & 3D models.
Azimkhon — Animation & design.
Zafar & Fazliddin — Mini-game development.

We combine creativity, research, and technology to make space exploration engaging for everyone.
summary:
AstroNex is an educational project dedicated to preserving and sharing the stories behind NASA’s space missions and technologies.

We developed a website featuring accessible explanations, 3D models, and interactive mini-games. Instead of simply collecting facts, we tell the stories of these machines from different perspectives: what they were designed to do, what they discovered, how their technologies contributed to scientific progress, and why their achievements still matter.

To reach a wider audience, we also created an Instagram channel where we share engaging, easy-to-understand video stories for people of different ages.

By combining interactive learning with visual storytelling, AstroNex makes space exploration more accessible and helps ensure that the achievements of these missions are not forgotten.
details:
Project Overview

AstroNex is an educational web project focused on preserving and sharing the stories of NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. Our goal is to make the achievements of these machines understandable and memorable, even after their missions have ended.

How It Works

Visitors can explore interactive globes of the Moon and Mars, select real landing and mission sites, and discover the spacecraft, landers, and rovers associated with them. Each mission has its own educational page featuring accessible explanations, historical information, technical details, scientific discoveries, and 3D models that visitors can rotate and examine.

To make learning more engaging, we also developed three mini-games inspired by real space exploration stories. In addition, our Instagram channel extends the project beyond the website through short educational videos about space technologies and missions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AstroNex brings information from different official NASA resources together in one accessible place. Instead of presenting visitors with complicated technical documents, we turn scientific and historical information into understandable stories.

Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity about space exploration, make scientific knowledge more accessible to younger and non-expert audiences, and preserve the achievements of missions that might otherwise be forgotten.

Tools, Technologies and SI Assistance

We developed the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js and model-viewer for interactive 3D experiences. Blender was also used in the 3D modeling workflow.

SI tools played a significant role throughout our development process. We used ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini for a wide range of tasks, including brainstorming, research assistance, organizing information, writing and improving educational content, coding, debugging, problem-solving, and developing project ideas.

Different team members used these tools in different ways. ChatGPT supported research, fact-checking workflows, project planning, documentation, and educational content development. Claude assisted extensively with website development, coding, implementation, improvements, and the creation of videos for our Instagram channel. Google Gemini was used by Zafar to help develop one of the mini-games, which was subsequently further improved with Claude's assistance.

We treated these tools as assistants rather than replacements for our team's work. Our members made project decisions, directed the development process, reviewed outputs, and checked scientific information against official NASA, JPL, and other relevant sources. We aimed to distinguish verified facts from interpretations and avoid presenting unverified information as scientific fact.

Creativity and Key Considerations

Our creative approach combines interactive exploration, 3D visualization, educational storytelling, and mini-games. Rather than simply listing facts, we help visitors understand where these machines went, what they did, what they discovered, and why their missions mattered.

Throughout development, we prioritized scientific accuracy, accessibility, usability on desktop and mobile devices, and transparency. We provide direct source links on mission pages and aim to make space exploration understandable even to visitors without a scientific background.

AstroNex is built around one central belief: when a mission ends, its story should continue.

Abandoned, but not Forgotten.
